acceptance.integrity_blocks: any pinned digest mismatch, any conflict rate > 0.5% of primary rows, or OTHER > 0
open_conditions: no fuzzy or name-derived mapping (the matcher never reads names)

crosswalk_source.name: pinned nflverse weekly rosters 2023-2024 (identity columns gsis_id, pfr_id, team, season, week, game_type only)

columns_never_used: everything else in players.csv (status, last_season, latest_team, draft, height, ...)
identity_source.extract_rule: rows with both gsis_id and pfr_id non-blank, sorted by tuple, csv LF, gzip level 9 mtime 0 (pure function of the source bytes; see nfl_v2_phase1p_identity_sources.extract_bytes)
identity_source.historical_usage: Rolling upstream file; its bytes changed on the day of retrieval. Reproduction therefore reads only the committed digest-verified extract and never downloads a latest file. Only the id pair is used for matching; display_name is carried for unmapped-row forensics and never used to match.
identity_source.name: nflverse players dataset (players.csv)

mapping_rule.ambiguity: a pfr_id with more than one gsis id in any single accepted source stays unmapped (AMBIGUOUS_PFR_TO_GSIS)
forbidden: targets, carries, yards, scores, snaps in the target game, participation or any outcome to infer identity
hierarchy: 1. exact canonical pfr_id -> gsis_id (frozen extract), unique gsis
2. exact pinned-roster pfr_id -> gsis_id, unique gsis
3. when both exist they must agree exactly; disagreement is SOURCE_CONFLICT and the row stays unmapped
mapping_rule.many_to_one: two distinct snap PFR ids resolving to the same gsis id inside the same (season, week, team) is SOURCE_CONFLICT for both rows

preregistration_note: The mapping hierarchy below is the one specified in the task brief. Before this protocol was committed the author had seen only that a canonical pfr_id -> gsis_id column exists in the nflverse players dataset and a preliminary aggregate coverage figure; no rule was tuned on unmapped rows and no player was patched.
question: Can exact, auditable skill-position snap-count PFR->GSIS mapping reach the preregistered 95% minimum without names, outcomes, target-game information or hindsight?

reason_classes.AMBIGUOUS_PFR_TO_GSIS: more than one gsis id for the pfr id in an accepted source
reason_classes.NO_CANONICAL_ID_RECORD: pfr id absent from both the canonical extract and the roster crosswalk
reason_classes.ROSTER_CROSSWALK_MISSING: pfr id appears on a pinned roster row with a blank gsis id and nowhere else
reason_classes.SOURCE_CONFLICT: canonical and roster disagree, or same-team-week many-to-one

reproducibility: Float shares use explicit division of integer counts; JSON is sorted-key and rounded to 6 decimals; no mutable file is read.
scope: DATA ENGINEERING ONLY. No role model is fitted. Identity and snap-source metadata only (season, week, team, name, PFR id, position, offense_pct).

snap_source.name: nflverse snap_counts release (pinned)
snap_source.population: regular-season rows with offense_pct > 0; primary positions WR,TE,RB,FB,HB; QB reported separately as a diagnostic and excluded from the gate
